scope: Whole program, same IO/compiler settings within each comparison; original APIs retained; online results refer to submitted baselines, not new code.

findings.classification: Same bounded-RMQ/LCA family; dominant construction/input-representation/general-feature and memory-layout cost, plus meaningful IO; not a simple O(log N) versus O(1) gap.
findings.own: General undirected-forest API: component/depth/subtree/ancestor metadata; depth<=256 bounded lifting, deeper trees 32-node RMQ plus ancestor ladder. get remains documented O(1) under the fixed depth cutoff.
findings.best: Problem-specialized parent array with p[i]<i and u<v; reverse-order subtree counts and preorder numbering without adjacency allocation, original parent-label RMQ in blocks of 64, within-block bounded scan. It does not provide the general forest/level-ancestor API.
findings.same_io_evidence: Random 500k/500k: own O2 114.421 ms, best core/main with own IO 40.858 ms; line 70.081 vs38.695; binary64.376 vs41.429. Representation/API breadth remains material after IO normalization.
findings.io_evidence: Own main/core with mapped toy IO: random98.108ms (0.857x), line57.164 (0.816x), binary47.747 (0.742x). Best full O2 random20.549ms versus own IO40.858ms. IO impact depends strongly on the core/main.
findings.construction_evidence: Instrumented random: input+adjacency25.240ms, LCA build41.981ms, query+IO40.470ms. Instrumentation changes code layout; phase values are diagnostic, not an exact additive split of the uninstrumented run.
findings.candidate_decision: Force existing RMQ for all depth>1: random1.159x and binary1.473x slower; reject. Omit ladder is query-only API-incomplete ablation: line0.899x, no adoption. Parent-input construction/packed representation is a future API-preserving design question; do not import narrower assumptions into general LCA.

findings.classification: Micro/macro packed index and XOR-tree construction, with substantial batch numeric IO and prefetch contribution; explicit SIMD kernel is a smaller separate contribution.
findings.own: General HLD forest representation and chain-based O(log N) jump, with O(1) same-chain case.
findings.best: Immutable tree-specific 16-byte vertex words, XOR-degree leaf peeling, macro chain prefixes, <=32-node micro masks; scalar/AVX2 mismatch/predecessor and BMI2 select, special path/star shapes. Main uses trusted bounded fields, regular-file mapped input, 64-query view, 8-query lookahead and bulk output.
findings.same_io_evidence: Random: own HLD204.075ms vs Fastest scalar index/direct query/own IO98.145ms (0.481x). Line81.880 vs75.275ms (0.919x), binary154.062 vs90.022ms (0.584x). This compares different index algorithms/representations on the same IO/compiler, not identical construction APIs.
findings.main_isa_ablation: Within the separate matched target/IO experiment: removing prefetch costs5.6–15.5%; scalar kernel versus AVX2 with prefetch off costs -0.9% to8.4%; removing the 64-record batch from same canard IO/index costs29.6–59.3% relative to no-prefetch batched view. All variants have equal output.
findings.candidate_decision: No repository candidate. If continuing, assess compact jump-specific index and batching as distinct features; retain standard fallback and CPU dispatch for any adopted SIMD. Do not transplant Fastest fixed CPU target/regular-file-only assumptions into the library by default.

findings.classification: Different algebra-specific algorithm plus implementation/layout and IO. HLD split range sums have O(log² N) worst-case; root-prefix method with LCA and subtree endpoint Fenwick updates has O(log N) with an O(1) or O(log N) LCA.
findings.own: Both owned and callback entries use HLD plus Fenwick over DFS-ordered original vertex values. Owned API additionally fuses some Fenwick access. range() must continue to expose original DFS values.
findings.best: Euler subtree endpoint updates maintain current root-to-vertex sums in a difference Fenwick; LCA is a compact 64-block RMQ. Query is rootSum(u)+rootSum(v)-2rootSum(lca)+value(lca). Parent input/output use mapped word parsing and decimal tables.
findings.same_io_evidence: Random: owned257.574ms, callback277.628ms, best core/main+own IO138.784ms. Balanced:219.862/227.634 vs90.634ms. Line:98.278/96.542 vs106.407ms; Best does not dominate every shape.
findings.io_evidence: Owned main/core with toy mapped IO: random237.009ms (0.920x), binary204.248 (0.929x), line78.454 (0.798x). IO alone cannot explain random gap.
findings.independent_algorithm_reference: A temporary root-prefix formula using the unchanged own HLD/Fenwick/IO APIs passes all small naive and large baseline checks, but random263.347ms, balanced195.691ms, line131.624ms versus owned257.574/219.862/98.278. It only helps some shapes; asymptotic change alone does not reproduce Fastest constants/construction.
findings.candidate_decision: Do not change internal Fenwick contents or range() contract. The reference is a separate algorithm experiment, not a replacement Verify for path_prod. Any specialized invertible-group/root-path API is a later design decision.

findings.classification: Worst-case HLD decomposition/aggregation structure dominates the official maximum; IO matters on other shapes. Fastest fuses heavy paths with biased auxiliary balanced trees and shared forward/reverse affine aggregation.
findings.own: General Ordered HeavyLightValues with standard segment-tree queries over HLD fragments and two directional range states; point update and path aggregate are generic noncommutative operations.
findings.best: Problem-specific static heavy-path/auxiliary-tree construction; priority derives from index interval bits; forward/reverse affine aggregate shares one multiplicative coefficient and two offsets. It integrates traversal and aggregation instead of invoking an independent range query per fragment. The logn source label suggests logarithmic aggregate traversal; this report does not supply a formal complexity proof.
findings.official_case_evidence: Official worst generators seed0/1 reproduced input SHA and own raw output SHA exactly. Same GCC15.2 O2: own205.622/208.354ms, own+toy IO191.441/197.520ms, best+own IO129.355/133.009ms, best full113.313/114.219ms. Core/structure gap remains ~36–37% after IO normalization; IO-only swap saves ~5–7%.
findings.shape_evidence: Synthetic random own91.165ms vs best+own IO86.644ms; line own46.325 vs66.298ms, so replacing the general structure is not a universal improvement. Official max worst cases explain the online241vs116ms ranking.
findings.candidate_decision: Do not copy Fastest code into repository. A fused/biased static-tree aggregator would be a new implementation/design requiring generic API, reverse-order, ownership and exception validation. Preserve existing API as the reference baseline.

library_checker_five_others.scope: Latest own LC submissions versus fastest snapshots for five problems. No online mutation/rejudge/submission; no third-party solver implementation compiled/copied into repo.
library_checker_five_others.compiler_caveat: API only exposes lang=cpp per submission. Current official catalog says C++23 GCC15.2+ACL1.6; the exact compiler build/hardware/rejudge date of old submissions is not exposed, so online time ratios are whole-program observations, not controlled core-only comparisons. Local comparisons explicitly use /usr/bin/g++15.2, CPU11, same input/prefix/I/O unless an identified candidate component changes.
library_checker_five_others.measurement_caveat: Judge score is maximum case time, and max case may differ. Tiny-case ratios below 5ms suppressed. New local timings do not predict online AC or exact judge time.
